config.prompt: Two unifications, one method — pair each piece with its role:

pairs.right: became the engine of Italy — diplomacy, volunteers and plebiscites
became the engine of Germany — three short, calculated wars
nations built from barricades — and lost
unification from above: existing states captured the nationalist movement

config.why: The two strands interlock anyway: Italy gains Venetia in 1866 only because Prussia defeats Austria, and Rome falls in 1870 only because France is busy fighting Prussia.

activities.name: uni1848Buckets

config.prompt: Why 1848–49 failed in Italy — file each piece of evidence:

items.label: Radetzky's veterans beat every coalition thrown at them
Venice's republic starved into surrender, August 1849
republicans and monarchists had no common plan
the Pope refused to lead a war on Catholic Austria
the revolutions were urban and middle-class; most peasants stayed home
even France intervened against an Italian republic

config.why: Yet one outcome mattered enormously: Piedmont alone kept its constitution — the Statuto — the one liberal, constitutional Italian state, and hence the lesson of the 1850s: a state, not a street, would make Italy.

activities.anchor: The masterstroke was the secret pact of Plombières
activities.caption: line up Cavour's road, earliest first
activities.name: uniCavourOrder

config.prompt: The statesman's road — order the steps, earliest first:
items: An army corps of some 15,000 sent to the Crimean War — 1855
'The Italian question' presented at the Congress of Paris — 1856
The secret pact of Plombières with Napoleon III — July 1858
Victories at Magenta and Solferino; Lombardy gained — 1859
Villafranca: Napoleon III signs the peace alone; Venetia stays Austrian — 1859
Plebiscites in Tuscany, Parma, Modena and the Romagna join Piedmont — March 1860
config.why: Industrialise, buy a seat at the top table, then fight — and when the emperor's nerve failed, consolidate by plebiscite. France took Nice and Savoy as its price.

activities.anchor: His stated aim in 1859 was a Kingdom of Upper Italy
activities.caption: drag the divider — aim, then outcome
activities.name: uniAimCompare

config.prompt: The plan and what actually happened — drag the divider:

before.label: The stated aim, 1859
before.text: A Kingdom of Upper Italy — Piedmont plus Lombardy-Venetia plus the duchies, with the Pope keeping Rome.

after.label: What events produced
after.text: The whole peninsula, improvised above all by Garibaldi — Cavour died in June 1861, three months after the proclamation, with Venetia and Rome still missing.

config.why: He helped with an army, a legal framework of plebiscites and international respectability; he hindered by ceding Nice, first trying to stop the expedition, and channelling everything into a conservative monarchy with no place for Mazzini's republicans.

activities.anchor: In May 1860 he sailed from Quarto with the
activities.caption: call the number — the Thousand
activities.name: uniThousandEstimate

config.prompt: Garibaldi's 'Thousand' — roughly how many red-shirted volunteers actually sailed from Quarto?
config.why: 1,089, many of them students and artisans — yet victory at Calatafimi against a larger force, the fall of Palermo despite a garrison of some 20,000, and a Bourbon army of some 100,000 dissolved by desertion and defeat.
config.context: The expedition could only sail because Cavour's annexations had destabilised the map.

activities.anchor: He conquered the south — about a
activities.caption: find the faulty line — who made Italy
activities.name: uniGaribSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Garibaldi conquered the south — about a third of the new state.
The north was won by Cavour's diplomacy and the regular Piedmontese army.
The centre was joined by plebiscites held after Piedmontese troops marched in.
Victor Emmanuel's army crossed the Papal States, beating papal forces at Castelfidardo.
In 1870 France sent fresh troops to defend the Pope, and Rome was stormed.
config.correction: With France fighting Prussia in 1870, its garrison protecting the Pope went home; Bersaglieri breached the walls at Porta Pia, 20 September 1870.
config.why: Even Garibaldi's later attempts on Rome failed — wounded by Italian troops at Aspromonte (1862), checked at Mentana (1867). Rome fell in the end to diplomacy; Venetia had arrived in 1866, as Prussia's ally.

config.root: 1865. You are Bismarck. The real target is Austria — but Prussia cannot be strong everywhere at once. What do you secure before the confrontation?

start.text: Three neighbours matter before the Bund can be defied.

choices.label: Russian goodwill
choices.feedback: Prussia had helped crush the 1863 Polish revolt — Russia stands aside.

choices.label: French neutrality
choices.feedback: Biarritz, October 1865: vague promises of 'compensation' never defined buy France out.

choices.label: An Italian alliance
choices.feedback: April 1866: Venetia dangled as the price — Austria now faces two fronts.

russia.text: Russia stands aside. When the Bund votes to mobilise on 14 June 1866, Bismarck declares it dissolved and marches — Moltke's railways and needle guns decide the Seven Weeks' War.

france.text: France stays out. When the Bund votes to mobilise on 14 June 1866, Bismarck declares it dissolved and marches — three Prussian armies converge on Bohemia.

italy.text: Austria fights on two fronts. When the Bund votes to mobilise on 14 June 1866, Bismarck declares it dissolved and marches.

config.why: Königgrätz (3 July 1866): roughly 250,000 Prussians against some 200,000 Austrians and Saxons — Prussian losses about 9,000, Austrian about 44,000 including 20,000 captured. Bismarck then annexed the north-German states that had opposed him.
